name: Low block and counter-attack
scopeNote: Idea, not one team: absorb pressure in a compact deep or mid block, concede possession, and attack space in transition with fast forwards. Sources use 'counter-attack', 'mid-block', 'deep block', 'non-possession-based strategy'. Window covers the two exemplars: Mourinho's Inter 2009/10 (Barcelona semi-final 20 and 28 April 2010, Bayern final 22 May 2010) and Ranieri's Leicester 2015/16 (season ended 15 May 2016). Not 'catenaccio' (man-marking libero), which is a separate catalog ideology; Maldonado shows Inter mixed zonal block with man-marking of Messi. Manager spell dates are from memory and not verified in the digests (Mourinho at Inter 2008-06-02 to 2010-05-28; Ranieri at Leicester 2015-07-13 to 2017-02-23). Leicester evidence comes mostly from tier C press/Premier League site; no tier A study of Leicester found.
openQuestions: No team/leicester-2015-16 or manager/claudio-ranieri research file exists yet; ids proposed in exemplars are new and need creating or confirming.

Is Leicester 2015/16 a deep 'low block'? FM-type sources say deep block; Premier League says two banks of four, 4-4-1-1 out of possession, and 42.43% possession. No source quantified defensive line height.

Man-marking vs zonal at Inter: Maldonado says Messi 'man-marked everywhere he went' with Pandev tucking in to man-mark, while other web summaries call it zonal with shared responsibility; Mourinho's Coaches' Voice masterclass body not read (only intro).
Inter second leg (10 men, 24% possession) was an extreme low block; first leg and final are the more counter-attacking examples.
Leicester pressing and set-pieces not covered by a verified fact.
